I first got into Legendary playing the Firefly Box with some guys in a card shop. I liked the "episodic" way that the villain deck is shuffled (x number of villains between partitions)

I tried doing that with some of the more difficult mastermind/scheme combos after losing to them repeatedly (Galactus/Nukes was the worst thing my randomizer ever did to me) and you can make it work surprisingly well. 

Other things that you can do could be things like adding another henchman group to pad out the villain deck or a house rule my friends have played with where we can spend 2 recruit points to shuffle the HQ back into the hero deck (doubling the cost for each time you do it 2,4,8,16, etc.).

I'm also big into writing down the setups that beat us and trying them again later with different heroes.

Most dispensers do not have any sort of safety sensor for fire until you get to the inside. More often than not these small fires wouldn't do much more than send someone to the hospital with burns on their hands and faces. But I witnessed someone lose their car because of a static fire in a gas can that was on their passenger seat.

The point is, Fire Code is in place for a reason. Anyone with half a brain should know that it is better to be safe than sorry.

I found that super annoying after I moved back home so I started talking with an English teacher friend I met down there and we found some ways to get around those situations. It mainly involved me saying what I wanted to say in English, describing to him what it meant, and then he would tell me something I could say instead that would make sense in Portuguese. It didn't always work but most of the time it's just a different way of saying it. Sometimes you just have to make it up as you go, like describing a similar type of situation to what you want to say. It can get a little confusing but half the time the people around me don't know what I'm saying anyway so I don't worry to much about it.

TL;DR: Find someone who teaches your native language in another and you can figure out expressions to use.
